algorithm: Reject edge counts below n-1 or above n(n-1)/2. The smallest possible diameter is zero for a singleton, one for a complete graph with at least two vertices, and two otherwise. Compare this minimum strictly with k-1.
correctness_argument: A connected simple graph needs at least n-1 edges and has at most one edge per unordered pair. For n>1, diameter one is equivalent to being complete. Every other admissible edge count is achieved by a star plus arbitrary unused edges. This construction has diameter at most two, and its missing edge forces diameter at least two. These lower bounds and constructions give the exact minimum used in the strict comparison.
edge_cases: n=1 requires m=0 and has diameter zero.
A complete graph with n>1 has diameter one.
